title: Identify Which Companies Visit Your Website and What They Read
summary: See which companies read your website, which pages and where they came from: Snitcher resolves each visit to an organisation, two Cargo models keep the companies and their sessions current, and the tracker loads only after a visitor accepts. How it works, the fields, the cost per identified company, and what it will not do.
body_markdown:
**To identify which companies visit your website and what they read, resolve each visit’s IP address to an organisation with Snitcher and keep the results in two Cargo models: one row per visiting company, and one per session with its pages and referrer.** The site loads the tracker only after a visitor accepts it, and nothing identifies a named person.


The[visitor-identification cookbook](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/visitor-identification) declares that setup for a site hosted on Cargo. This page covers what happens between a page view and a row, what the rows mean, what it costs and what it deliberately does not do.


## Deploy it#


The site has to exist first, usually from[website-building](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/build-and-host-your-company-website-on-your-own-domain) . Then, inside that Cargo project:


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com


cargo-ai   project   add   cookbook/visitor-identification
cargo-ai   project   plan
cargo-ai   project   deploy


```


` project add` writes the two models to` infra/visitor-identification/` and copies the site files (the consent gate, the loader and` visitors.json` ) next to the procedure in` .claude/skills/visitor-identification/` . Your coding agent then wires them into the website app: render the gate from the layout, hand the app the tracker snippet as an env token, and point the banner at your privacy page.


## How it works, end to end#


1. **A visitor accepts tracking.** The site renders its own banner with equal “Accept tracking” and “Reject tracking” buttons. Before a choice, after a rejection, and under Global Privacy Control, the page makes no request to Snitcher at all.
2. **The site loads its own loader.** It takes only the public profile ID from Snitcher’s snippet and loads the tracker with reviewed settings: consent required, and form, click, download, error and recording capture off. An unrecognised snippet fails the build.
3. **Snitcher resolves the visit.** The IP address is matched to the organisation that owns it.
4. **Cargo syncs the rows.**` website_visiting_companies` uses the Snitcher` fetchOrganisations` extractor, and` website_visitor_sessions` uses` fetchSessions` . Both fetch incrementally on Cargo’s own interval, at most every 30 minutes, and refuse a cron.


The wiring is one deploy. Creating the companies model provisions a Snitcher workspace for your site URL and writes two values into the model’s config:` _trackingScript` , which the website app receives as` NEXT_PUBLIC_SNITCHER_SNIPPET` , and` _workspaceUuid` , which the sessions model reads. Both are deploy-time references, so they resolve in the same deploy that creates them.


Tracking runs only on the canonical origin of a site marked` ready` . The Cargo URL, previews and a draft site load nothing.


## What comes back#


Model One row per Fields


` website_visiting_companies` organisation resolved from a visit` name` ,` website` ,` industry` ,` size` ,` founded` ,` address` ,` profiles` ,` first_seen` ,` last_seen`


` website_visitor_sessions` visit by an identified company` organisation_uuid` ,` started_at` ,` ended_at` ,` referrer` ,` device_type` ,` location` ,` views` (each with` url` ,` visited_at` ,` time_on_page` )


Join them on` organisation_uuid = uuid` to see which companies read your pricing page this week. Check the live column names with` cargo-ai storage column list` before you rely on a query; the extractor owns them.


Read the counts honestly. Visitors who reject send nothing, many addresses never resolve to an organisation (home broadband, mobile networks), and a shared office, VPN or coworking network resolves to whoever owns the address. A day with no identified company is a valid zero.


## What it needs#


- A website on Cargo hosting with an HTTPS canonical URL, and` @cargo-ai/cdk` 1.0.98 or later.
- The workspace’s default Snitcher connection, on Cargo’s credits. No Snitcher account or API key: the managed path provisions the tracker. A workspace on its own Snitcher key selects an existing workspace instead and provisions nothing.
- A privacy page you have reviewed that describes Snitcher, the purpose and the retention. The build fails while` privacyPolicyUrl` is empty and tracking is on; the cookbook never writes legal text.


## What it costs#


Each identified company is billed **3 credits** once, when it first lands in the companies model. Sessions cost **0** . That is the list price in the Snitcher integration’s definition; read it live with` cargo-ai connection integration get snitcher` before the first deploy. Spend follows your traffic and there is no built-in cap, so agree to it up front. Removing the companies model stops the billing.


## What it will not do#


- **Identify people.** No identify call, no email capture, and no named person inferred from a visit. A row is a company.
- **Load anything before consent.** Snitcher’s own` waitForConsent` still records page views before consent, which is why the gate does not request the script until the visitor says yes.
- **Contact anyone.** Nothing is sent. Acting on a visit (a score, an alert, an email) is your decision, and anything that does has to say it is about the company.
- **Keep the history if the URL changes.** A new` url` on the companies model provisions a new Snitcher workspace with a new tracker and an empty history.


## Questions#


The cookbook is written for a site on Cargo hosting, because the snippet reaches the site as an app env token in the same deploy. The models themselves are ordinary Snitcher models; on another host you would load the tracker yourself, behind your own consent mechanism.


No. Call the loader from your CMP’s grant event and its deny path from revocation instead of rendering the gate, then re-test that nothing loads before a grant and after a withdrawal.


Not out of the box. The cookbook lists it as a variation: a segment over the companies model joined to your target list, with an alert on new rows. The alert has to say it is a company, because a visit says someone on that network read the page, not who.


Deploy it from the[visitor-identification cookbook](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/visitor-identification) . To turn the visitors who do identify themselves into leads, see[turn website visitors into routed, qualified leads](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/turn-website-visitors-into-routed-qualified-leads) .
